figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic overview of the dataset generation and validation pipeline. The workflow comprises four stages: Procedure: After prescreening, participants provided informed consent, completed practice, and underwent formal EEG recording, followed by subjective ratings on representative sound clips. Preprocessing: EEG recordings were preprocessed according to standardized procedures. Validation: EEG data validation included signal quality assessment (layout verification, bad-channel analysis, ICA analysis), neurophysiological plausibility checks (PSD validation), and decoding performance evaluation. Behavioral validation included analyses such as excluded-trial summaries, reaction time distributions, and subjective rating assessments. Release: All data, including metadata, raw and processed EEG recordings, stimuli, subjective ratings, and processing scripts, were publicly released in a structured format.

Figure 2. (a) The EEG experimental setup. (b) Hardware configuration and data flow. (c) Overview of the experimental procedure.

Figure 3. Directory layout of the SAAD-EEG dataset as released on Zenodo. Icons indicate item types: g directories, j raw EEG recordings (.mff), Ð JSON metadata, O tabular files (.tsv), and A other release files (.md/.npy). Only sub-01 is shown in full. Ellipses (...) indicate repeated structures across participants and sessions. Under each main audio category in stimuli/wav/, grey italic text lists the two subcategory folder names.

Figure 4. Signal quality assessment results for the SAAD-EEG dataset. (a) Sensor layout of the 128-channel HydroCel EEG system. (b) Number of interpolated channels and excluded ICA components for each participant. (c) Representative independent components identified by ICA and labeled with ICLabel. (d) EEG signals at representative electrodes F1, Fz, and F2 before and after artifact removal. (e) Group mean PSD (dB) over 1–40 Hz for the pre-stimulus baseline (-3 to 0 s; dashed grey) and dichotic-stimulus (0 to 2 s; solid red) windows. Shaded regions indicate the standard error of the mean (SEM) across participants. (f) Scalp topographies of the stimulus-minus-baseline log-power difference (dB) for theta, alpha, and beta bands, averaged across participants. (g) Robustness of EEGNet decoding for each participant across three cross-validation schemes: trial-random, mirror-constrained, and category-held-out splits. The dashed horizontal line indicates chance level.

Figure 5. Behavioral analysis results for the SAAD-EEG dataset. (a) Number of excluded trials for each participant. (b) RT distributions for three sessions across all participants. (c) Group-level selection rates for music, speech, high-ecology, and low-ecology sounds in the dichotic listening stimulus-driven attention task. Each bar shows the ratio of trials in which a category was selected to trials in which it was available as the left- or right-ear stimulus. The dashed line at 0.5 indicates chance performance (no systematic bias). Gray asterisks mark categories whose selection rates differ significantly from 0.5; the horizontal bracket and label indicate that all pairwise comparisons between categories are significant. Bonferroni correction (α = 0.05) was applied separately to each test family. (d) Pair-level logistic regression (binomial GLM, logit link). Odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals for left–right audio-feature differences and group-level selection on one side of each stimulus pair. The dashed vertical line indicates OR = 1; ∗p < 0.05, ∗∗p < 0.01, ∗∗∗p < 0.001. (e) Mean subjective ratings across participants (familiarity/liking/urgency; 0–4 scale) of representative clips for each subcategory.
